documents.title: Analytics Portal Solution Design
documents.description: Logical solution design for the fedc Analytics Portal, covering the platform roles of Oracle Analytics Cloud, Databricks Lakehouse, and the Confluent iPaaS orchestration layer, with a sequence diagram illustrating the end-to-end data flow from CC&B to business user.
documents.scope: Analytics Portal — the self-service BI surface and underlying data pipeline from Oracle CC&B through Confluent and Databricks to Oracle Analytics Cloud. Aligned to SVI-001 and ADR-013.
documents.overview: The Analytics Portal solution is composed of three primary platform components: Oracle Analytics Cloud (PLAT-BI) as the self-service BI and reporting surface; the Databricks Lakehouse (PLAT-LAKEHOUSE) as the governed data storage and transformation tier; and the Confluent iPaaS (PLAT-IPAAS) as the event orchestration layer that moves data from Oracle CC&B into the lakehouse in near-real-time. Oracle Analytics Cloud connects to the lakehouse via a Databricks SQL endpoint (JDBC). Unity Catalog enforces row- and column-level security so that operational and commercial users access only datasets appropriate to their role. Scheduled batch ingestion supplements event-driven flows for MDM and ERP source systems.

solution-components.role: Self-service analytics portal — provides workbooks, subject areas, dashboards, and natural language querying for operational and commercial business users. Connects to the Databricks lakehouse via JDBC SQL endpoint. Hosts the fedc Semantic Model (governed metrics, KPIs, and dimensions).
solution-components.notes: Oracle Analytics Cloud 23.x. OAC Data Gateway deployed in the fedc AWS VPC to bridge OAC SaaS to private Databricks SQL endpoint.

solution-components.role: Enterprise data lakehouse — stores raw (bronze), cleansed (silver), and curated (gold) Delta tables. Unity Catalog provides data governance, lineage, and access control. Gold-layer tables are exposed to OAC via the Databricks SQL serverless endpoint.
solution-components.notes: Databricks on AWS. Unity Catalog with three catalogues: ops_catalogue (operational datasets), commercial_catalogue (commercial and financial datasets), regulatory_catalogue (Ofgem settlement and RIIO-ED2 datasets).

solution-components.role: Event orchestration layer — Confluent Kafka receives CC&B change-data-capture events via the Debezium Oracle connector, routes them through transformation topics, and delivers them to Databricks Auto Loader via the Databricks Kafka connector. Also orchestrates scheduled batch ingestion triggers for MDM and ERP.
solution-components.notes: Confluent Cloud on AWS (same region as Databricks). Schema Registry enforces Avro schema compatibility. Event retention: 7 days on operational topics, 90 days on regulatory topics.

solution-components.role: Primary operational data source — Oracle CC&B provides billing, account, payment, and service order data via change-data-capture (LogMiner-based Debezium connector). CC&B is read-only from the lakehouse perspective; no write-back.
solution-components.notes: Oracle CC&B version 2.9. Debezium Oracle CDC connector deployed on a dedicated Kafka Connect cluster in the fedc data centre DMZ.

data-flows.name: CC&B Operational Data CDC Flow
data-flows.description: Near-real-time change-data-capture flow from Oracle CC&B to the Databricks Lakehouse bronze layer, covering billing account changes, payment events, and service order updates.
steps: Oracle CC&B writes a billing or account change transaction to its Oracle DB (CC&B schema).
Debezium Oracle CDC connector (running on Kafka Connect) reads the change from Oracle LogMiner and publishes an Avro-encoded change event to the Confluent topic ccb.billing.account.changes.
Confluent Schema Registry validates the Avro schema version against the registered schema for ccb.billing.account.changes.
A Kafka Streams transformation processor applies field-level masking to PII fields (name, address) before routing to the downstream topic ccb.billing.account.changes.masked.
Databricks Auto Loader (Kafka source) consumes events from ccb.billing.account.changes.masked and appends records to the bronze Delta table ops_catalogue.raw.ccb_billing_accounts.

A Databricks DLT (Delta Live Tables) pipeline runs on a 10-minute trigger, transforming bronze records into the silver table ops_catalogue.cleansed.billing_accounts applying deduplication and schema enforcement.

A second DLT pipeline aggregates silver data into the gold table ops_catalogue.reporting.billing_kpis, computing metrics including Days Sales Outstanding, payment failure rate, and unread meter percentage.
Oracle Analytics Cloud queries the gold table via the Databricks SQL serverless endpoint (JDBC) and renders updated KPIs in the Operational Dashboard workbook for business users.

data-flows.name: MDM Batch Ingestion Flow
data-flows.description: Nightly batch ingestion of Oracle MDM meter register data into the Databricks Lakehouse, providing a daily snapshot of the active meter estate for use in regulatory and commercial reporting.
steps: A Confluent scheduled connector triggers an Oracle MDM REST API export at 01:00 UTC, requesting a full snapshot of active meter records.
Oracle MDM returns a paginated JSON response containing meter attributes, location, configuration, and lifecycle status.
Confluent OIC adapter transforms the MDM JSON response to Avro and publishes records to the Confluent topic mdm.meters.snapshot.
Databricks Auto Loader consumes the snapshot topic and overwrites the bronze Delta table ops_catalogue.raw.mdm_meters using REPLACE WHERE partition = current_date.
A DLT pipeline applies MDM business rules (meter type classification, voltage normalisation) to produce the silver table ops_catalogue.cleansed.meters.
The gold table ops_catalogue.reporting.meter_estate_summary is refreshed, providing counts by meter type, region, and lifecycle status for regulatory reporting.

uml-diagrams.title: CC&B to Analytics Cloud Data Flow
uml-diagrams.description: End-to-end sequence diagram showing data movement from Oracle CC&B through the Confluent event backbone and Databricks Lakehouse to Oracle Analytics Cloud and the business user.
uml-diagrams.content:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CIS as Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS)
    participant CDC as Debezium CDC Connector
    participant Kafka as Confluent Kafka (PLAT-IPAAS)
    participant SR as Schema Registry
    participant DBX as Databricks Lakehouse (PLAT-LAKEHOUSE)
    participant OAC as Oracle Analytics Cloud (PLAT-BI)
    participant User as Business User

    CIS->>CDC: Write billing/account change (LogMiner)
    CDC->>SR: Validate Avro schema
    SR-->>CDC: Schema OK
    CDC->>Kafka: Publish change event (ccb.billing.account.changes)
    Kafka->>Kafka: PII masking transformation (Kafka Streams)
    Kafka->>DBX: Auto Loader consumes masked events
    DBX->>DBX: Append to Bronze Delta table (raw.ccb_billing_accounts)
    DBX->>DBX: DLT pipeline: Bronze -> Silver (cleansed.billing_accounts)
    DBX->>DBX: DLT pipeline: Silver -> Gold (reporting.billing_kpis)
    User->>OAC: Open Operational Dashboard workbook
    OAC->>DBX: JDBC query via Databricks SQL serverless endpoint
    DBX-->>OAC: Return gold-layer KPI rows
    OAC-->>User: Render dashboard with up-to-date metrics

interface-requirements.notes: CDC via Oracle LogMiner. Target latency: events published within 60 seconds of DB commit. Throughput: up to 50,000 events/hour during billing cycle peak.
Databricks Auto Loader in Kafka mode with incremental checkpointing. Triggered continuously; commits micro-batches every 10 minutes.

interface-requirements.data-format: SQL over JDBC (Databricks SQL serverless endpoint)
interface-requirements.notes: OAC Data Gateway (deployed in fedc AWS VPC) proxies JDBC queries from OAC SaaS to the private Databricks SQL endpoint. Authentication via OAuth2 service principal.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: CC&B operational data must be available in the gold layer of the Databricks Lakehouse within 15 minutes of the originating transaction being committed in Oracle CC&B.
non-functional-requirements.rationale: ADR-013 target: reduce operational information lag from 24 hours to under 15 minutes for critical operational KPIs.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: The end-to-end pipeline (PLAT-CIS → PLAT-IPAAS → PLAT-LAKEHOUSE) must achieve 99.5% availability during business hours (07:00–22:00 UK time).
non-functional-requirements.rationale: Operational dashboards are used by contact centre and field operations teams throughout the business day.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: The Confluent cluster and Databricks Auto Loader must handle 3x current peak event volume (150,000 events/hour) without degradation, to accommodate smart meter rollout event growth.
non-functional-requirements.rationale: Smart meter estate is projected to grow from 800,000 to 2.5 million endpoints by 2028, significantly increasing CC&B event volumes.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: PII fields (customer name, address, contact details) must be masked at the Confluent transformation layer and must not be present in Databricks bronze or silver tables. Gold-layer tables may surface pseudonymised identifiers only.
non-functional-requirements.rationale: UK GDPR data minimisation principle. Databricks analytics users should not have access to raw PII.

assumptions.description: Oracle LogMiner is enabled on the CC&B Oracle DB instance and the DBA team has confirmed supplemental logging is active on the relevant billing and account tables.
The Databricks SQL serverless endpoint is available in the AWS region being used for the fedc Databricks workspace.

open-questions.question: Should the OAC Semantic Model (metrics and dimensions) be built in OAC's native semantic modeller or sourced from a dbt semantic layer on Databricks? This affects where business logic resides and which team owns metric definitions.

What is the agreed approach for handling schema evolution on the ccb.billing.account.changes Avro topic — backward compatibility only, or full compatibility? This determines whether CC&B schema changes require a Kafka topic migration.

documents.title: CRM Integration Solution Design
documents.description: Logical solution design for the integration between Salesforce CRM (PLAT-CRM) and Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS), enabling a unified agent desktop with embedded billing context and event-driven proactive outbound communications.
documents.scope: CRM-to-CIS integration — covering the synchronisation of account and billing data between Salesforce CRM (PLAT-CRM) and Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS), mediated by Oracle Integration Cloud (PLAT-IPAAS). Aligned to AVI-002 (Digital Customer Experience Vision).
documents.overview: The CRM Integration solution mediates between Salesforce CRM (the system of record for customer interactions and cases) and Oracle CC&B (the system of record for billing accounts). Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) is used as the API orchestration layer for synchronous account lookup requests from Salesforce, and as the event consumer for CC&B billing events (via Confluent Kafka) that trigger proactive outbound communications in Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The integration replaces the existing bespoke Java middleware and establishes a governed, observable integration layer.

solution-components.role: Salesforce CRM acts as the customer engagement system of record. Agents use a Salesforce Lightning component to view embedded billing summary data retrieved in real-time from CC&B via OIC. Salesforce Marketing Cloud triggers proactive outbound communications (email, SMS) based on CC&B billing events consumed via Kafka.
solution-components.notes: Salesforce Sales Cloud + Service Cloud + Marketing Cloud. Lightning Web Component for embedded billing summary (Salesforce Canvas or OIC REST API call-out).

solution-components.role: Oracle CC&B is the system of record for billing accounts, payment history, and service agreements. CC&B exposes account data via its REST API (CC&B Service Layer) to OIC. CC&B billing events (payment failures, estimated reads, disconnection warnings) are published to Confluent Kafka via the existing Debezium CDC connector.
solution-components.notes: CC&B Service Layer REST API — authenticated via service account. Rate limit: 500 requests/minute from OIC.

solution-components.role: Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) orchestrates synchronous account lookup requests: receives a REST call from Salesforce, calls CC&B Service Layer, transforms the response to a Salesforce-compatible JSON payload, and returns it. OIC also acts as a Kafka consumer for CC&B billing events, transforming and routing them to Salesforce Marketing Cloud REST API for outbound communication triggers.
solution-components.notes: OIC Generation 3. Two integration flows: (1) CRM-to-CIS Account Lookup (synchronous REST-to-REST), (2) CIS Billing Event to Marketing Cloud Trigger (Kafka-to-REST async).

data-flows.name: Agent Billing Context Lookup
data-flows.description: Synchronous lookup of billing account summary from CC&B when a Salesforce agent opens a customer record, providing real-time balance, payment status, and last meter read within the Salesforce UI.
steps: Salesforce agent opens a customer Account record in Salesforce Service Cloud.
A Salesforce Lightning Web Component (embedded billing panel) fires an Apex callout to the OIC REST endpoint /cis/account/{accountId}/summary.
OIC validates the request (service account auth), maps the Salesforce account ID to the CC&B account number via a cached cross-reference table.
OIC calls the CC&B Service Layer REST API GET /api/v1/accounts/{ccbAccountId}/summary.
CC&B returns account summary JSON (balance, last payment date, last meter read, service agreement status).
OIC transforms the CC&B response to the Salesforce billing panel schema and returns it to the Lightning Web Component.
The Salesforce billing panel renders the account summary inline within the agent's customer record view.

data-flows.name: CC&B Payment Failure Proactive Notification
data-flows.description: Event-driven flow from CC&B payment failure event through Confluent and OIC to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, triggering a proactive outbound email and SMS to the customer within 4 hours of the payment failure.
steps: Oracle CC&B records a payment failure on a billing account (direct debit return or card decline).
Debezium CDC connector publishes a ccb.payment.failure event to the Confluent Kafka topic ccb.billing.events with Avro payload including account ID, failure reason, and amount.
OIC Kafka consumer adapter polls ccb.billing.events, filters for event type PAYMENT_FAILURE, and initiates the Proactive Notification integration flow.
OIC queries Salesforce CRM REST API to retrieve the customer's communication preferences (email/SMS opt-in status and language preference) using the cross-referenced Salesforce Contact ID.

OIC calls the Salesforce Marketing Cloud REST API (Transactional Messaging) to trigger the PAYMENT_FAILURE journey with the customer's communication preferences and account details as personalisation data.
Salesforce Marketing Cloud sends the outbound email and/or SMS to the customer within the 4-hour SLA window.
OIC logs the notification dispatch event to the integration audit log (OAC observability topic) for Ofgem Consumer Duty reporting.

uml-diagrams.title: Agent Billing Context Lookup — Sequence
uml-diagrams.description: Synchronous sequence for the Salesforce agent billing context lookup via Oracle Integration Cloud to CC&B.
uml-diagrams.content:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent as Salesforce Agent
    participant SF as Salesforce CRM (PLAT-CRM)
    participant OIC as Oracle Integration Cloud (PLAT-IPAAS)
    participant CIS as Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS)

    Agent->>SF: Open Customer Account record
    SF->>OIC: POST /cis/account/{accountId}/summary (OAuth2)
    OIC->>OIC: Resolve Salesforce ID -> CC&B Account Number (cache)
    OIC->>CIS: GET /api/v1/accounts/{ccbAccountId}/summary (service account)
    CIS-->>OIC: 200 OK — account summary JSON
    OIC->>OIC: Transform CC&B response to Salesforce billing panel schema
    OIC-->>SF: 200 OK — billing panel payload
    SF-->>Agent: Render billing summary panel in UI

interface-requirements.notes: Salesforce Apex callout to OIC REST endpoint. Timeout: 10 seconds. Authentication: OAuth2 client credentials.
OIC calls CC&B Service Layer REST API. Service account authentication. Rate limit: 500 requests/minute.

interface-requirements.direction: PLAT-IPAAS → PLAT-CRM (outbound to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, async)
interface-requirements.data-format: JSON (REST — Salesforce Marketing Cloud Transactional Messaging API)
interface-requirements.notes: OIC calls Salesforce Marketing Cloud REST API after consuming CC&B billing events from Confluent. Async fire-and-forget; OIC logs dispatch confirmation.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: The agent billing context lookup (DF-001) must complete within 3 seconds end-to-end (Salesforce callout to OIC to CC&B and back) under normal load.
non-functional-requirements.rationale: Contact centre UX requirement: agents cannot wait more than 3 seconds for billing panel to render before the call experience degrades.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: CC&B payment failure events must trigger Salesforce Marketing Cloud notification dispatches within 4 hours of the originating payment failure event.
non-functional-requirements.rationale: Ofgem Consumer Duty requirement for proactive customer communication. ADR-013 target.

non-functional-requirements.requirement: The Kafka consumer (OIC) must process payment failure events with at-least-once delivery semantics. Duplicate suppression must be applied using the CC&B event ID as an idempotency key.
non-functional-requirements.rationale: A missed payment failure notification constitutes a Consumer Duty breach. Duplicates are preferable to missed notifications but must be suppressed to avoid customer confusion.

assumptions.description: A cross-reference mapping table between Salesforce Account/Contact IDs and CC&B Account Numbers is maintained in OIC's lookup table store and is kept current by the existing Salesforce-CC&B account matching process.
Salesforce Marketing Cloud is licensed and configured with the PAYMENT_FAILURE transactional journey template and the customer communication preference data extension.

open-questions.question: Should the OIC cross-reference lookup table (Salesforce ID to CC&B Account Number) be cached in OIC or synchronised to a shared Redis cache? At contact centre scale (500 concurrent agents), OIC lookup table read performance needs to be validated under load.
